LD 305 -- "An Act Regarding Transportation in Maine"

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and members of the Transportation
Committee -- good afternoon, my name is Anya Trundy, Deputy Commissioner for
the Department of Administrative and Financial Services. I am testifying at the
request of the Administration Neither For Nor Against LD 305, "An Act Regarding
Transportation in Maine."
This testimony pertains to the sponsor's proposed amendment to the LD 305
concept draft. The amendment, which is retroactive to May 30, 2025, adds an automobile lessee to the exemption of excise tax and the maximum number of
automobiles exempt from the excise tax for certain veterans. The amendment
requires, if there are multiple lessees of an automobile, that at least one lessee
whose name appears on the lease agreement is eligible for the excise tax
exemption.
Under 36 M.R.S. �1483, sub-�12, certain disabled veterans are entitled to
exemption fiom the motor vehicle excise tax. This exemption has historically
required, and currently requires, ownership of the vehicle by the veteran. This proposal would create the only excise tax exemption under section �l483 that
applies to leased vehicles.
Furthermore, it is unclear how refunds would be identified and distributed
for excise tax already paid on automobiles that would be retroactively exempt, and

the bill would likely impose additional administrative burdens on municipalities
and/or the State to process and document retroactive refunds. We strongly
recommend that if the Committee chooses to move forward with this bill the changes made by the bill not be applied retroactively. Changing the effective date
to October l, 2026, would greatly simplify the bill's administration while still
accomplishing its core objectives.
The preliminary fiscal impact estimate is not available at this time, but the bill would have an impact on local tax receipts. The bill's administrative costs will
depend on how refunds are administered, and the exact cost estimate is under
review.
The Administration looks forward to working with the Committee on the
bill.

February 3, 2026 Testimony of Rep. Lydia Crafts presenting
LD 305, An Act Regarding Transportation in Maine
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
Good afternoon, Senator Nangle and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Transportation. My name is Lydia Crafts, and I represent House District 46, which includes
Bristol, Damariscotta, Monhegan Plantation, Newcastle and Nobleboro. Today, I am pleased to
present LD 305, An Act Regarding Transportation in Maine.
Last session, this committee updated the disabled veterans' exemption to make the program more targeted. In doing so, the program unintentionally excluded veterans who qualify for the program
except that they lease their vehicles rather than own. This update was brought to me by the good
Representative from Oakland and he can provide real-life examples from his community.
I ask that this committee maintain the emergency preamble and make the policy change retroactive, to make right the unintended negative consequences for those disabled veterans.
Thank you for your time and I am happy to answer any questions.

District 46 Bristol, Damariscotta, Newcastle, Nobleboro and Monhegan Plantation

10059611:
Testimony in Support of LD 305: "An Act Regarding Transportation in Maine"
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and the distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation, my name is Montana Towers, and I serve as policy analyst for Maine Policy Institute. Maine Policy is a free market think tank, a nonpartisan, nonprofit organization that advocates for individual liberty and economic freedom in Maine. Thank you for the opportunity to submit testimony in support of LD 305, "An Act Regarding Transportation in Maine"
The proposed bill would ensure that veterans who qualify for free vehicle registration under Maine law, and who are recognized by the U.S. government for total serviceconnected disability, are eligible for the same excise tax exemption for leasing a vehicle as they are for purchasing one.
Public policy should not penalize individuals for choosing the most practical or affordable option available to them, especially not veterans who have borne the cost of defending our nation. For many disabled veterans living on fixed incomes or disability compensation, leasing a vehicle offers the most reasonable and accessible path to safe, reliable transportation. To exclude them from tax relief based solely on ownership structure is counter to the very spirit of the original law.
Maine Policy Institute has long supported reforms to Maine's vehicle excise tax system. This bill represents a common-sense correction to ensure consistency and fairness in how these taxes are applied.
Importantly, the bill preserves safeguards to ensure that only qualified veterans receive the exemption by requiring their name to appear on the title or lease. This maintains program integrity while ensuring that no eligible veteran is left behind due to an arbitrary technicality.
In conclusion, this amendment reflects good governance: it acknowledges a legislative oversight, acts swiftly to fix it, and does so in a way that restores fairness without expanding bureaucracy or creating new entitlements.
For these reasons, Maine Policy Institute strongly urges this committee to vote "Ought to Pass" on LD 305. Thank you for your time and consideration.

JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORTATION
L.D. 305 An Act Regarding Transportation in Maine
Testimony of Shenna Bellows, Secretary of State and Cathie Curtis, Deputy Secretary for the Bureau of Motor Vehicles,
Department of the Secretary of State
February 3, 2026
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and Distinguished Members of the Transportation Committee, I am providing testimony neither for nor against L.D. 305 "An Act Regarding Transportation in Maine."
As amended by the sponsor's amendment, L.D. 305 provides an excise tax exemption for certain veterans who drive a leased vehicle (or two or three). While the payment of excise taxes and registration fees are often co-mingled in drivers' minds, we do not administer or receive the excise tax (municipalities do); therefore, we do not take a position on whether or not an excise tax exemption is appropriate. Should the committee decide to include registration fee exemptions for leased vehicles, we stand ready to work with the committee on language. We note that retroactivity would create serious and costly implementation problems.
Thank you for your time and I would be happy to answer your questions.

member service organization and aims to help provide policy solutions that Work for all residents in Maine.
The LPC guides MMA's advocacy efforts and establishes positions on bills of municipal interest.
MMA's LPC will likely acknowledge the importance of parity for disabled veterans when it comes
to the motor vehicle excise exemption afforded to vehicle owners. The primary concerns we would like to
raise at this time are the retroactivity of this provision and the continued erosion of municipal funding streams. Expanding exemptions to tax programs in Maine, even Worthy ones, transfers costs to average property taxpayers. Revenue streams are eroded by exemptions, but the underlying costs do not go away.
Given the unprecedented nature of the proposal to retroactively provide this exemption, ' MMA's
LPC will undoubtedly inquire asto the source of funding for these reimbursements and the administration
of this work. Is this work that the state will be taking on, should this bill pass as amended?

The retroactive application` of the exemption proposed would create an administrative and budgetary
burden on municipalities if so assigned. Notably, providing refunds retroactively could "impact audited
financials. MMA's LPC will likely suggest amending the bill to remove the retroactive provision.

MMA will submit additional information to the committee after the LPC meeting next week. Thank
